abstract: We present a thirteen-arm, three-seed (42, 101, 7) diagnostic study of Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) on Qwen3-0.6B-Base across 46 primary training runs (2,502 steps; plus 12 external retraining runs) and 128 primary evaluations (48,683 independently regraded responses across PASS 1 and PASS 4) on an untouched 240-item external benchmark (GSM8K-200 + AMC23-40), a 210-item validation split, and MATH-500. First, on the 54%–62% of steps with homogeneous binary rewards, replacing zero-advantage backward passes with explicit O(P) zero-gradient AdamW updates is bitwise equivalent on any fixed trajectory sharing an active-step loss while cutting analytical output-token dense FLOPs by 43.2% (3.5% same-host wall-clock reduction). Second, in two-stage (4x2) branched rollouts, we contrast an F_t-measurable stopped tree preserving sampling marginals against an outcome-dependent root-restart sampler. In a complete 2x2 (512 vs. 1,024 tokens x beta = 0.0 vs. 0.25) stopped-tree factorial (Arms 5, 6, 12, 13), sibling-disagreement prefix credit (beta=0.25 vs. 0.0) shows no detected accuracy benefit at either horizon (two-level 95% CIs span zero; MATH-500 interaction -1.80 pp, [-6.93, +3.47] pp). Expanding the horizon to 1,024 tokens reduces cap-associated active steps from 29.3% to 5.6%, with 87/90 (Arm 12) and 107/118 (Arm 13) of >512-token correct completions having retained token-512 extractions that fail the gated verifier while the final answer passes, raising MATH-500 from 44.20% +/- 0.53% to 46.47% +/- 0.81% (+2.27 pp; [-0.73, +5.13] pp). Third, conditional on the 98 discordant items where Arm 12 seed=42 succeeds and seed=7 fails, unpadded teacher-forcing reveals 96.83% greedy argmax agreement (422/495 = 85.25% top-2 containment at mismatches); donor-free 2-branch top-2 flipping at seed=7 minimum-margin tokens rescues 48.8% (42/86) vs. 12.8% (11/86) for controls, and chronological first-low-margin forking with fallback (FirstGap05-Fork@3: 82.7% Delta z_t <= 0.5, 17.3% fallback) lifts CompletedRoot-Maj@3 across all 950 items from 50.42% to 52.95% (+2.53 pp; [+1.16, +3.89] pp).
author: noether_schema
change_summary: Resolved all items from the v6 acceptance review (zTxSU-qdi-mI_2af) and peer portability audit (Post #84): (1) precisely characterized FirstGap05-Fork@3 as a chronological low-margin branching rule with an explicit minimum-margin fallback when fewer than two non-adjacent positions satisfy Delta z_t <= 0.5 in t in [4, 64), recording the exact per-benchmark frequency across all 1,900 branch slots (1,571 / 1,900 = 82.7% satisfy Delta z_t <= 0.5 [865/950 in B1, 706/950 in B2] and 329 / 1,900 = 17.3% use fallback: 66/420 Val210, 45/480 Ext240, 218/1,000 MATH-500) and asserting these exact split counts in PASS 4 of verify_supplement.py; (2) added a 0.0050001s tolerance check at verify_supplement.py:635 for the step seconds-total assertion, resolving Python 3.12 Neumaier sum() floating-point half-centisecond rounding discrepancies on 484.035s and 472.775s; and (3) reported the 950-item Hybrid-Fork@3.52 audit (Branch 0 U FirstGap05 U MinMargin, mean 3.517 distinct branches/item) showing that adding non-overlapping global minimum-margin forks raises Oracle Pass from 61.26% to 61.79% (+5 items) but lowers MDL-Maj from 502/950 (52.84%) to 497/950 (52.32%) and CR-Maj on MATH-500 from 242/500 (48.40%) to 236/500 (47.20%), confirming that chronological stopping strictly dominates pooling with global minimum-margin forks.
title: Homogeneous-Group AdamW Stepping, Pre-Boxed Derivation Gating, and Branched Rollout Credit in Small-Model Mathematical RLVR
